_comment: APPROVE — Destin looks at a change that is ALREADY BUILT and answers Yes, keep it / No, revert it / Other.
Two screenshot sweeps: 'before' is master, 'after' is your branch. The rig boxes the pixels that differ.
Copy this file beside your design notes, rename it, replace every value. Every _comment is stripped when the deck is built, so leave or delete them as you like.
title: Send button — two changes to keep or revert
_comment_title: title: what this deck is about, in his words. It heads every page.
_comment_key: key: a short name for this deck. His answers are saved under it, so keep it stable across rounds.
_comment_out: out: the page build writes, beside this spec.
_comment_images: images: where the cropped pictures land. It must contain this file's own name, or two decks overwrite each other's pictures.

runs._comment: runs: the two screenshot sweeps to compare, as folders relative to this file. Make them with run-review.sh, once per branch.

_comment_themes: themes: which palettes every picture is shown in. Two is plenty unless colour is the point; six is the full set.

steps._comment: One step is one point. Keep a deck under about eight, or he stops reading.
steps._comment_id: id: your name for this point. It labels his answer, so keep it short and never reuse it.
steps._comment_surface: surface: the part of the app this lives in, named the way he would name it.
steps.path: The row under the message box
steps._comment_path: path: how he would get there — the screen, the menu route, the row.
steps._comment_crop: crop: which region of the screenshot to show. Names come from crops.json; add your own under a top-level "crops" block.
steps.headline: The send button now sits on its own line, clear of the model name.
steps._comment_headline: headline: the one sentence he reads first. What he SEES, not what you edited. 25 words at most, no code words.
steps.changed: The button moved down into a row of its own instead of sharing the row with the model name.
steps._comment_changed: changed: the What changed card. One or two sentences on the real difference.
steps.measured: 24 px lower, 8 px clear of the model name
steps._comment_measured: measured: a number that proves it — sizes, counts, milliseconds. Leave it out when you have none; a number with no digit is refused.
steps.notice: Nothing overlaps when the model name is long, and the button no longer jumps as you type.
steps._comment_notice: notice: the You'll notice card. What is different for him while he is using it.
steps.risk: The message box is 24 px shorter, so a long message scrolls a line sooner.
steps._comment_risk: risk: the Risk card. What could go wrong or annoy him. Leave it empty when there is genuinely nothing.

steps._comment: A second point, showing the two optional fields a step may carry.
steps.path: The strip along the bottom of the window
steps.headline: The bottom strip keeps one line of text instead of wrapping to two.
steps.changed: Long branch names are shortened in the middle now, so the strip never grows a second line.
steps.notice: The window stops shifting up and down while a session runs.
steps.risk: A very long branch name reads as its start and its end with a gap in the middle.

highlight._comment: highlight: what the box goes around. Omit it on a two-run deck and the rig boxes whatever pixels changed. Use "text" for words on screen, or a hand-placed "box": [x, y, w, h] as a last resort.

steps._comment_themes: themes on a STEP: show this one point in fewer palettes than the deck — for a surface captured in only one.
